questions.a: A wise person is someone who is able to understand difficult matters.

questions.q: What does Qoheleth advise about the king?
questions.a: Qoheleth advises people to obey the king, because of the oath they swore before God.

questions.q: How should people whom the king has ordered to do something wrong respond?
questions.a: People should not be afraid and should not stand in support of something wrong but should leave the king’s presence immediately in order to protect themselves.

questions.q: Who can question what the king does?
questions.a: No one can question what the king does, because his word is authoritative.
Whoever keeps the king’s commands avoids harm.
For every matter there is a proper time and way to do it.

questions.q: What can no one tell a person?
questions.a: No one can tell a person what will happen in the future.

questions.q: Over what does no one have power?
questions.a: No one has power over the wind, and no one has power over the day of his death.

questions.q: What did Qoheleth see about people’s authority over others?
questions.a: Qoheleth saw that sometimes a person has authority over another and uses it to harm them.

questions.q: By whom were the wicked praised?
questions.a: The wicked were praised by people in the city where they had done their wicked deeds.

questions.q: What happens when punishment for evil deeds is not given quickly?
questions.a: When punishment for evil deeds is not given quickly, many people feel tempted to commit evil deeds without fear of consequences

questions.q: Even if a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives for a long time, what will happen to those who fear God?
questions.a: Even if a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives for a long time, it will be good for those who fear God and honor him.

questions.q: What will happen to the wicked person who does not fear God?
questions.a: It will not go well for the wicked person, and he will not lengthen his days, because he does not fear God.

questions.q: What sometimes happens to righteous people on earth?
questions.a: Sometimes righteous people seem to experience the bad things that the wicked people deserve.
Qoheleth recommends happiness because humanity has no better thing to do than to celebrate life and be happy.

questions.q: What did Qoheleth give his heart to know?
questions.a: Qoheleth gave his heart to know wisdom and to see the business that is done on the earth.
Humanity cannot understand everything that God does on the earth.

commentary.text: Commendations of wisdom. (Eccl. 8:1-5) To prepare for sudden evils and death. (Eccl. 8:6-8) It shall be well with the righteous, and ill with the wicked. (Eccl. 8:9-13) Mysteries of Providence. (Eccl. 8:14-17)

Eccl. 8:1-5 None of the rich, the powerful, the honourable, or the accomplished of the sons of men, are so excellent, useful, or happy, as the wise man. Who else can interpret the words of God, or teach aright from his truths and dispensations? What madness must it be for weak and dependent creatures to rebel against the Almighty! What numbers form wrong judgments, and bring misery on themselves, in this life and that to come!

Eccl. 8:6-8 God has, in wisdom, kept away from us the knowledge of future events, that we may be always ready for changes. We must all die, no flight or hiding-place can save us, nor are there any weapons of effectual resistance. Ninety thousand die every day, upwards of sixty every minute, and one every moment. How solemn the thought! Oh that men were wise, that they understood these things, that they would consider their latter end! The believer alone is prepared to meet the solemn summons. Wickedness, by which men often escape human justice, cannot secure from death.

Eccl. 8:9-13 Solomon observed, that many a time one man rules over another to his hurt, and that prosperity hardens them in their wickedness. Sinners herein deceive themselves. Vengeance comes slowly, but it comes surely. A good man's days have some substance; he lives to a good purpose: a wicked man's days are all as a shadow, empty and worthless. Let us pray that we may view eternal things as near, real, and all-important.

Eccl. 8:14-17 Faith alone can establish the heart in this mixed scene, where the righteous often suffer, and the wicked prosper. Solomon commended joy, and holy security of mind, arising from confidence in God, because a man has no better thing under the sun, though a good man has much better things above the sun, than soberly and thankfully to use the things of this life according to his rank. He would not have us try to give a reason for what God does. But, leaving the Lord to clear up all difficulties in his own time, we may cheerfully enjoy the comforts, and bear up under the trials of life; while peace of conscience and joy in the Holy Ghost will abide in us through all outward changes, and when flesh and heart shall fail.
